minorInfoFindings.title: Trajectory "throttle" field records the commanded control, not the effective throttle actually used by step()
minorInfoFindings.detail: run() at sim.mjs:172-176 pushes record(t, s, u) where `u` is the raw controller output, while step() (sim.mjs:50-51) silently forces `throttle = 0` whenever state.fuel <= 0. The recorded throttle is therefore not the throttle that produced the recorded physics. Reproduced with a synthetic flameout run (controller always commands throttle 1): 1596 of the trajectory records have fuel == 0 together with throttle == 1, e.g. {"t":31.3,"x":156.5,"y":4430.3383,"vx":5,"vy":101.4268,"theta":0,"fuel":0,"throttle":1} — a record that claims full thrust while the vehicle is in pure free fall. The shipped autopilot never empties the tank (189.42 kg left), so the acceptance path is unaffected, but index.html manual mode hits this as soon as the player holds throttle up after flameout (index.html:289 uses the same record(simTime, sim, currentU)), and the same value drives the flame at index.html:412, so the lander would visibly burn fuel-less thrust on screen.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Have step() return the effective throttle it used (e.g. expose `throttle: throttle` on the returned state, or a second value) and pass that into record() instead of the raw command; in run(): `const s2 = step(s, u); if (i % recordEvery === 0) trajectory.push(record(t, s2, { throttle: s2.effThrottle, torque: u.torque }));`. Also use the effective throttle for the flame length in index.html. (Cross-cutting: the same fix repairs the visual flame.)

minorInfoFindings.title: Autopilot control-law comment is 12 lines, spec asks for 3-5
minorInfoFindings.detail: SPEC: "its control law must be commented in 3-5 lines". The autopilot documentation block at sim.mjs:77-88 is 12 comment lines (77-88) before `export function autopilot(state)` at line 89. Content itself is accurate and complete (desired-velocity schedule, PD on velocity error, theta_des = atan2(ax, ay+g), throttle = mass*|T|/MAX_THRUST, PD on tilt) — it is only the length that overshoots the stated budget. Flagging it here because it lives in sim.mjs; it may overlap the autopilot dimension's grading.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Collapse the block to 5 lines or fewer, e.g. one line for the vy/vx schedule, one for the velocity-PD -> desired accel, one for theta_des = atan2(ax, ay+GRAVITY) and throttle = mass*|T|/MAX_THRUST, one for the tilt PD torque, one for the clamps; move the longer rationale into README.md.

minorInfoFindings.title: Spec numbers 300 s and recordEvery=6 are duplicated as literals in index.html instead of exported from sim.mjs
minorInfoFindings.detail: The two remaining spec-mandated numbers are run() defaults only (sim.mjs:159-164: `maxTime = 300, recordEvery = 6`) and are not exported, so index.html re-hardcodes them: line 291 `if (sim.y <= 0 || simTime >= 300 - DT / 2)` and line 289 `if (mode === 'manual' && stepCount % 6 === 0)`, plus the display string at line 223 `(limit 300 s)`. All of the FIXED physics constants themselves are correctly shared (index.html imports run/autopilot/step/judge/record/initialState/LIMITS/PHYSICS_PANEL/DT/MAX_ANGULAR_ACCEL/MAX_ANGULAR_RATE/BURN_RATE from './sim.mjs' at lines 128-131, and a grep found no duplicated 1.62/3000/500/250/90/45 physics literals in index.html), so this is not a physics-source duplication — it is the same single-source-of-truth risk for the sim-limit numbers, which can silently drift if run() defaults change.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Export `export const MAX_SIM_TIME = 300; export const RECORD_EVERY = 6;` from sim.mjs, use them as the run() defaults, and import them in index.html for the stop condition and sampling; also return the effective touchdown record from run() so manual mode can use identical sampling.

minorInfoFindings.title: clamp() passes NaN through, so a non-finite control poisons the entire state
minorInfoFindings.detail: sim.mjs:33 `const clamp = (v, lo, hi) => (v < lo ? lo : v > hi ? hi : v);` — both comparisons are false for NaN, so clamp(NaN,0,1) === NaN. Observed: step(START_STATE, {throttle: NaN, torque: 0}) returns {"x":null,"y":null,"vx":null,"vy":null,"fuel":null} (JSON rendering of NaN), and the NaN then propagates forever through run(). Not reachable from the shipped UI (manualControl clamps at index.html:190/191-193 and autopilot is closed-form), and the spec defines controls as already being in range, so this is robustness only — but it is the one way the "controls are clamped" guarantee can be bypassed.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Guard non-finite inputs in step(): `const raw = Number(control.throttle); let throttle = clamp(Number.isFinite(raw) ? raw : 0, 0, 1);` and the same for torque, optionally asserting Number.isFinite on the incoming state.

minorInfoFindings.title: Spec-literal fuel clamp gives one step of thrust for fuel that no longer exists
minorInfoFindings.detail: sim.mjs:65-66 implements the spec text exactly (`fuel -= throttle*BURN_RATE*DT; if (fuel <= 0) fuel = 0;`), which means on the transition step the vehicle can receive full thrust while burning less than the commanded propellant (up to BURN_RATE*DT = 0.1333 kg of "free" impulse, e.g. state.fuel = 0.0005 with throttle 1). This is faithful to the specification's own wording and ordering, so no change is required — recorded only so the reviewer knows it was examined rather than missed. The alternative (proportionally capping thrust with the remaining propellant) would deviate from the spec.
minorInfoFindings.fix: None — keep as-is. If physical propellant conservation is ever wanted, it must be a spec change, not a code change.

minorInfoFindings.title: run() seeds the trajectory at t=0 and only includes touchdown when steps % 6 == 0; manual mode does not
minorInfoFindings.detail: sim.mjs:169-176 pushes an initial record at t=0 and then every 6th step, so length == floor(steps/6)+1 (verified: 130 records for the shipped 774-step run, 3001 for the 18000-step timeout run). Because 774 % 6 == 0, the shipped autopilot's final record is exactly the touchdown state ({"t":12.9,"x":7.8159,"y":-0.0197,"vx":-0.7719,"vy":-1.5105,"theta":0.157,"fuel":189.4183,"throttle":0.4338} vs final {"x":7.815920870668295,"y":-0.01973405921296111,...}) — the vy-at-touchdown cross-check against the last two recorded points holds to 2.4e-4 m over 6 steps. For an arbitrary control law (e.g. manual flight in index.html:289, which starts sampling at stepCount 6 with no t=0 point) the touchdown state may be absent from the copied JSON. Spec only requires sampling every 6th step, so this is an observation about traceability, not a violation.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Optionally append a final record for the touchdown/timeout state in run() (and mirror it in index.html's manual path) and push the t=0 point, keeping the identical 8-field format, so the exported JSON always ends at the verdict.

minorInfoFindings.title: Run-loop thresholds (300 s timeout, y <= 0 touchdown, recordEvery 6) are duplicated in index.html rather than exported from sim.mjs
minorInfoFindings.detail: sim.mjs owns the loop rules: maxTime = 300 and recordEvery = 6 as run() defaults (sim.mjs:162-163), the stop predicate `while (s.y > 0 && t < maxTime - DT / 2)` (sim.mjs:171), and `landed = s.y <= 0` (sim.mjs:178). index.html re-derives the same rules with literals: `if (mode === 'manual' && stepCount % 6 === 0)` (index.html:289) and `if (sim.y <= 0 || simTime >= 300 - DT / 2)` (index.html:291); the '(limit 300 s)' strings are also hard-coded in the banner (index.html:223), in test.mjs:28 and inside sim.mjs's own TIMEOUT message (sim.mjs:129). Integration math is NOT duplicated, so this is drift/config hazard rather than a physics fork (hence minor, not critical): if run()'s maxTime or recordEvery ever changes, the browser's stop condition and sampling cadence silently disagree with the headless run that the README claims is identical.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Export the loop config from sim.mjs (`export const MAX_TIME = 300; export const RECORD_EVERY = 6;` used as run()'s defaults) and ideally a predicate `export function isTerminal(state, t) { return state.y <= 0 || t >= MAX_TIME - DT / 2; }`. index.html:289-291 then uses stepCount % RECORD_EVERY and isTerminal(sim, simTime); index.html:223 and test.mjs:28 interpolate MAX_TIME.

minorInfoFindings.title: index.html recomputes the step count from time/DT instead of reusing the steps value run() already returns
minorInfoFindings.detail: run() returns `steps: i` (sim.mjs:181, verified: 774 at t = 12.90 s), yet the RUN AUTOPILOT handler recomputes `stepCount = Math.round(res.time / DT)` (index.html:237). The two agree today, but this re-derives authoritative state the shared module already supplies, is sensitive to floating-point accumulation of simTime, and stepCount is what gates manual-mode trajectory sampling (index.html:289).
minorInfoFindings.fix: At index.html:237 use the shared result directly: `simTime = res.time; stepCount = res.steps;`

minorInfoFindings.title: Autopilot control-law comment block is 12 lines; spec requires 3-5
minorInfoFindings.detail: Spec: 'its control law must be commented in 3-5 lines'. The autopilot doc comment occupies sim.mjs lines 77-88 = 12 physical lines (2 header lines 77-79 plus three numbered strategy items 80-88, of which items 1 and 3 each spill onto extra wrapped lines). The content is correct and matches the code (verified item-by-item against sim.mjs:93 vyDes, :95 vxDes, :102 thetaDes=atan2(tx,ty), :104 throttle=mass*hypot/MAX_THRUST, :106 torque PD), so documentation quality is not in question — only the stated length bound is exceeded. No functional impact; the autopilot itself is spec-compliant (deterministic, lands in 12.9 s).
minorInfoFindings.fix: Condense sim.mjs:77-88 to 5 lines, e.g. drop the 3-line header (77-79, already covered by the file header at lines 1-4) and compress each numbered item to a single line, keeping the load-bearing facts: vyDes = -clamp(0.30*y, 1.2, 11); vxDes = -clamp(0.10*x, ±2.5) * clamp(y/25, 0, 1); P-gain 0.85 on velocity error with ax ±1.6 / ay -1.0..3.2 clamps; thetaDes = clamp(atan2(ax, ay+GRAVITY), ±32); throttle = mass*|(ax, ay+GRAVITY)|/MAX_THRUST; torque = PD on tilt.

minorInfoFindings.title: Comment says 'PD on velocity error' but the law is proportional-only, and it omits the vxDes clamp that bounds pad-capture authority
minorInfoFindings.detail: sim.mjs:84 states '2. PD on velocity error -> desired accel (ax, ay)'. The implementation at sim.mjs:97-98 is axDes = clamp(kp*(vxDes - vx), -1.6, 1.6)*hGate and ayDes = clamp(kp*(vyDes - vy), -1.0, 3.2) — a proportional term on the velocity error with no derivative component (the attitude loop at :106 IS a genuine PD, so the comment is right there and wrong at :84). The comment also never mentions the ±2.5 m/s saturation of vxDes at sim.mjs:95; that saturation, combined with the ±1.6 m/s^2 axDes ceiling and the hGate fade below 25 m, is what caps horizontal capture authority and is the direct cause of the only non-spec failure mode I measured (perturbed start vx=+8 m/s touches down at x=31.28 m -> CRASHED 'OFF PAD: x = 31.28 m (limit 15)'). Not a spec violation (the fixed start state lands at x=7.816 m), but the comment currently misdescribes the law in a way that would hide this limit from a reader.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Reword sim.mjs:84 to 'P on velocity error (no D term) -> desired accel (ax, ay), clamped to ax ±1.6 m/s^2, ay -1.0..3.2 m/s^2' and add that vxDes is saturated at ±2.5 m/s, so pad capture degrades for |vx0| > ~6 m/s. Optionally raise the vxDes saturation (e.g. ±4) or the axDes ceiling to widen the basin; both are inside sim.mjs, which the hard rules forbid me to edit, so this is a suggested follow-up rather than a required change.

minorInfoFindings.title: Independent cross-check: spec start state is comfortably landable — two unrelated control laws both land
minorInfoFindings.detail: Before reading the autopilot body I designed my own law against the spec physics only (constant-decel sqrt braking reference + critically damped pad spring + gravity-cancelling specific-force split). It LANDED from the fixed start state on the first attempt and is itself deterministic (40/40 identical runs). The shipped autopilot lands on the same start state with all four touchdown numbers inside the win limits and 189.42 kg of fuel to spare, and generalizes: it landed in 16 of 18 perturbed probes I tried (vy=-20, theta=±25 deg, omega=+30 deg/s, y=200, fuel=60 kg), so it is a real state-feedback law, not a lucky fit to the nominal condition. No impossible-start-state finding.
minorInfoFindings.fix: None required. Keep xcheck.mjs in verify-scratch/ as a regression foil: if sim.mjs physics constants are ever edited, a divergence between the two independent controllers is an early signal.

minorInfoFindings.detail: The only console errors observed during the entire live session are two browser-automatic GET /favicon.ico requests returning 404 (one from http://localhost:8731 on first load, one from http://127.0.0.1:8951 after the harness reloaded the tab). index.html declares no <link rel="icon">, so the browser probes the default path. This is NOT app code and does not break any interaction, HUD field, or required visual element, but it means the 'zero console errors' check is not literally satisfied. No JS/module/runtime errors and no warnings were seen.
minorInfoFindings.title: favicon.ico 404 produces a console error on load
minorInfoFindings.fix: Add an inline favicon to silence the automatic request, e.g. in <head>: <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16'><text y='14' font-size='14'>🌙</text></svg>"> (or a data:, empty icon). Keeps the app offline/self-contained with no external file.

minorInfoFindings.detail: index.html imports MAX_ANGULAR_ACCEL, MAX_ANGULAR_RATE and BURN_RATE (line 130) but never uses them; the on-screen constants panel is rendered entirely from PHYSICS_PANEL (lines 148-153). grep confirms these three identifiers appear only on the import line. Harmless at runtime (tree-shaking is irrelevant for a single module) but it is dead code that a reviewer may flag, and it slightly obscures which values the UI actually depends on.
minorInfoFindings.title: Three imported sim constants are never used in index.html
minorInfoFindings.fix: Drop MAX_ANGULAR_ACCEL, MAX_ANGULAR_RATE, BURN_RATE from the import list on line 130 (keep DT, LIMITS, PHYSICS_PANEL, run, autopilot, step, judge, record, initialState which are all used).

minorInfoFindings.detail: manualControl (index.html lines 186-195) sets manualThrottle=1 while Space is held, but manualThrottle is a persistent accumulator: after Space is released, nothing lowers it, so throttle stays at 100% until ArrowDown is pressed. Observed live: after a Space tap the craft kept climbing at 100% and reached alt 2421 m. This satisfies the spec ('Space = full throttle') and is not a violation, but the non-obvious stickiness could surprise a reviewer filming manual mode.
minorInfoFindings.title: Manual throttle persists at 100% after releasing Space
minorInfoFindings.fix: Optional UX polish only: treat Space as momentary (set throttle=1 for the held frames but let it decay on keyup) or document the behavior in the hint text. No change required for spec compliance.

minorInfoFindings.detail: The Playwright MCP browser proxied/re-served the project from 127.0.0.1:8951 instead of the localhost:8731 I started, and reloaded the tab once (which reset the sim to IDLE and cleared a window.__t0 marker I had set). I confirmed via SHA-256 that 8951 serves byte-identical index.html and sim.mjs to the audited files, so every browser result here is valid against the real sources. Flagging so the determinism/verdict evidence is not misread as coming from a divergent copy.
minorInfoFindings.title: Browser verification ran against harness proxy 127.0.0.1:8951 (byte-identical files)
minorInfoFindings.fix: None needed for the app. Noted for audit transparency: results were validated against the exact audited files (matching hashes).

minorInfoFindings.title: Landing pad surface and "PAD" target caption are hidden behind the controls panel at the default desktop viewport
minorInfoFindings.detail: The pad is drawn around the horizon at groundY = H*0.84 (line 312): the tinted target strip occupies groundY..groundY+14 (line 368), the grey pad bar groundY-2..groundY+2 (line 370), the center crosshair groundY+7 (lines 382-383) and the "PAD" caption baseline groundY+26 (line 389). #controls is docked at bottom:58px (line 43). Measured live at 1440x900: groundY = 756, pad strip 756-770, caption 782, while #controls.getBoundingClientRect().top = 760 with left 360 / right 1080. The pad horizontally spans about 555-885 (sx(-15)..sx(15) at scale 11), so it sits entirely inside the panel footprint: the pad surface, the crosshair and the "PAD" label are all painted over by the button bar (see verify-scratch/vismy-auto-1440.png). Only the dashed boundary lines above the ground (groundY-16..groundY+16, lines 373-376) remain visible, so the 'marked target zone' reads as two floating ticks rather than a pad.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Raise the horizon so the pad band is clear of the dock, e.g. groundY = H * 0.74 (or reserve the band: groundY = min(H*0.84, controlsTop - 34) measured from the DOM), or move #controls to a left/right dock. Alternatively draw the pad marker above the ground line (negative offsets) so it can never be occluded.

minorInfoFindings.title: Horizontal camera does not keep the lander in frame; in manual mode it can silently exit the viewport
minorInfoFindings.detail: camera() (lines 311-317) guarantees vertical visibility via viewTop, but horizontally it only partially follows: camX = Math.max(-12, Math.min(12, sim.x * 0.6)) (line 315). Beyond |x| = 20 m the camera stops moving entirely, so sx(x) = W/2 + (x - camX)*scale grows without bound. At 1440x900 with scale near its 11 px/m cap the lander leaves the right edge at roughly x = 12 + (720-40)/11 = 74 m; the fixed start state has vx = +5 m/s, so ~15 s of uncorrected rightward drift in FLY MANUAL puts the lander off-screen with no indicator, edge arrow or clamp. The spec's 'camera follows the lander' is only honoured vertically.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Follow with full gain and clamp to keep the lander on screen, e.g. const camX = clamp(sim.x, -W/(2*scale) + 40/scale, W/(2*scale) - 40/scale) (or simply camX = sim.x and let the pad scroll), so sx(sim.x) is always within [40, W-40]. Also consider clamping scale so the pad stays visible together with the lander.

minorInfoFindings.title: COPY TRAJECTORY JSON copies a single seed point when clicked before any run; the empty-array fallback is unreachable dead code
minorInfoFindings.detail: resetSim() always seeds the array with one record: `trajectory = [record(0, sim, currentU)]` (line 201), and resetIdle() calls it on load (line 488). The copy handler's guard `if (!trajectory.length) { trajectory = run({...}).trajectory; }` (lines 263-265) can therefore never fire, because length is always >= 1. Consequence: in the initial IDLE state (or right after RESET) the button copies `[{"t":0,"x":0,"y":100,"vx":5,"vy":-10,"theta":0,"fuel":250,"throttle":0}]` and reports "COPIED 1 POINTS", not the trajectory array the spec refers to. The author's evident intent (fall back to the canonical autopilot run) is defeated by the seed push.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Track whether a run has actually happened (e.g. a `hasRun` flag, or keep `trajectory = []` in resetSim and push the seed only when stepping), and gate the guard on that flag instead of on `!trajectory.length`.

minorInfoFindings.title: Three imported constants are unused in index.html
minorInfoFindings.detail: The import list at lines 128-131 pulls in MAX_ANGULAR_ACCEL, MAX_ANGULAR_RATE and BURN_RATE, but a whole-file grep shows each of those identifiers occurs exactly once — on the import line itself (line 130). Only DT, LIMITS, PHYSICS_PANEL, run, autopilot, step, judge, record and initialState are actually referenced. Dead imports on a file whose whole point is a single shared physics source read as leftover scaffolding.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Drop the three unused specifiers from the import list (they already reach the screen via PHYSICS_PANEL), or use them to drive the RCS/flame visuals so the import is meaningful.

minorInfoFindings.title: Held keys are never released when the window loses focus, so manual throttle can stick
minorInfoFindings.detail: Keyboard state is a Set filled on keydown and drained on keyup (lines 177-184). There is no 'blur' or visibilitychange handler, so holding ArrowUp/W and then alt-tabbing (or pressing a browser shortcut) leaves the key in `keys`; manualControl() keeps adding 0.02/step (line 188) and the lander keeps accelerating with no visible key pressed. Same for a stuck torque key. This is a robustness nit in manual mode only; it cannot affect autopilot determinism.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Add `addEventListener('blur', () => keys.clear())` (and optionally visibilitychange) so released-off-window keys do not persist.

minorInfoFindings.title: HUD altitude reads as a negative number after touchdown
minorInfoFindings.detail: updateHUD() prints `sim.y.toFixed(2) + ' m'` raw (line 465). Because the run loop terminates on the step where y first crosses zero, the landed state carries y = -0.0166 m, so the telemetry panel shows "altitude -0.02 m" while the banner says LANDED (observed live in verify-scratch/vismy-auto-1440.png and in the DOM read). Physically honest but reads like a bug to a reviewer, and it is inconsistent with the renderer, which already clamps the drawing to max(sim.y, 0) (line 402).
minorInfoFindings.fix: Display `Math.max(0, sim.y).toFixed(2)` (or show 0.00 once mode === 'finished') so the altitude never goes negative on screen.

minorInfoFindings.title: Engine flame is rooted at the foot plane instead of the engine bell, so it appears to pass through the legs
minorInfoFindings.detail: In drawLander() the body bottom is at y = 1.2*s (fillRect(-1.5*s, -0.4*s, 3.0*s, 1.6*s), line 444) and the feet are at y = 2.0*s (lines 430-440), but the flame polygon starts at 2.0*s (moveTo/lineTo at 2.0*s, lines 415-424) — i.e. at the same plane as the foot pads, with the legs painted on top of its first 0.8*s. The requirement 'a flame whose length scales with throttle' is satisfied (L = (0.9 + 6.5*throttle)*s, line 413, monotonic and gated at throttle > 0.01), this is purely an anchoring/cosmetic point.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Start the flame at the body skirt, e.g. moveTo(-w/2, 1.25*s) / lineTo(0, 1.25*s + L), and draw it before the legs so the nozzle, not the foot pads, is its origin.

minorInfoFindings.title: Trajectory cadence (6) and the 300 s flight limit are re-typed literals in index.html rather than shared with sim.mjs
minorInfoFindings.detail: physicsStep() hardcodes `stepCount % 6 === 0` for the manual-mode trajectory (line 289) and `simTime >= 300 - DT / 2` for the timeout (line 291), duplicating run()'s `recordEvery = 6` and `maxTime = 300` defaults (sim.mjs lines 162-163, 171, 176). These are not the FIXED physics constants (the physics constants themselves are correctly single-sourced via PHYSICS_PANEL/LIMITS, so this is not a duplication-of-physics violation), but if either default were ever changed in sim.mjs the manual trajectory cadence and the manual/autopilot timeout boundary would silently diverge.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Export RECORD_EVERY and MAX_TIME from sim.mjs and import them in index.html (and use them as run()'s defaults), so the 6-step cadence and 300 s limit live in one place.

minorInfoFindings.title: Autopilot control-law comment is 12 lines; spec requires 3-5
minorInfoFindings.detail: Spec: "its control law must be commented in 3-5 lines". The block above `export function autopilot` is lines 77-88 — 12 lines (header + 2 intro lines + three multi-line numbered items). The content is accurate against the code (vyDes = -clamp(0.30*y,1.2,11), vxDes = -clamp(0.10*x,-2.5,2.5)*hGate, thetaDes = atan2(tx,ty), throttle = mass*hypot/MAX_THRUST, torque = PD on tilt), so the requirement is met in substance but exceeds the stated size bound.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Condense sim.mjs:77-88 to 3-5 lines (one line for the desired-velocity law, one for the PD, one for the throttle/aim inversion, one for the torque PD); optionally move the longer derivation to README.md, which has no length bound.

minorInfoFindings.title: COPY TRAJECTORY JSON copies a 1-row array on a fresh page; its empty-state guard is dead code
minorInfoFindings.detail: resetSim() seeds `trajectory = [record(0, sim, currentU)]` (line 201) and resetIdle() runs at startup (line 488), so the guard `if (!trajectory.length)` at line 263 can never be true — the autopilot fallback on lines 263-265 is unreachable. Clicking COPY before pressing RUN AUTOPILOT or REPLAY SLOW puts a single object `[{"t":0,"x":0,"y":100,...}]` on the clipboard, which contradicts README.md:31-33 ("identical to what test.mjs prints", 130 rows). Acceptance item (4)/(5) still pass; this is the button's half-implemented no-run-yet state.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Change the guard to a real "no run yet" test, e.g. `if (trajectory.length < 2 || mode === 'idle')` before line 266, or disable/grey the button until a run exists and label it `COPY AUTOPILOT TRAJECTORY JSON`.

minorInfoFindings.title: Trajectory/HUD record the commanded throttle, not the forced-to-0 throttle, so rows can read fuel:0 with throttle:1
minorInfoFindings.detail: step() zeroes thrust when the tank is empty at entry (line 51) but returns only the state, so run()'s recorder writes the raw command: `record(t, s, u)` (line 176) -> `throttle: r4(u.throttle)` (line 118). Verified by a 40 s full-throttle manual burn: rows `{"t":31.3,...,"fuel":0,"throttle":1}` and `{"t":40,...,"fuel":0,"throttle":1}` while the physics applied zero thrust (vy only gains gravity). index.html repeats the same reporting: HUD `ui.thr` uses currentU.throttle (line 470) and manual recording uses currentU (line 289), so manual play shows "100 %" throttle with an empty tank. The spec's per-step control is the throttle that was forced to 0, so the exported JSON misreports the control actually applied. Not reachable in the autopilot run (fuel never drops below 189.42 kg).
minorInfoFindings.fix: Have step() return the applied throttle (e.g. add `throttleApplied` to the returned object, or clamp and expose it) and make record()/HUD use it; failing that, in record() write `throttle: s.fuel <= 0 ? 0 : r4(u.throttle)`.

minorInfoFindings.title: Camera hard-clamps the lander's x to +/-12 m instead of following it; the lander leaves the canvas in manual flight
minorInfoFindings.detail: Spec: "Camera follows the lander but clamps at the ground" — the only permitted clamp is vertical. Line 315 `const camX = Math.max(-12, Math.min(12, sim.x * 0.6));` caps horizontal tracking at 12 m while the vertical follow (viewTop/scale, lines 313-314) keeps tracking indefinitely. Reproducing the mapping at 1440x900 with a mild manual profile (throttle 0.60 for 8 s then 0.42, no torque) puts the lander at sx = 1441 px — off the right edge — at t = 16 s (x = 80 m, y = 26 m), with a peak sx of 2470 px. Autopilot and replay stay inside x in [0, 7.82] m so the primary flows are framed correctly; the defect shows up only when the player deliberately flies far off-pad.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Drop the +/-12 clamp and track sim.x directly (keep only a lag/smoothing term), or clamp camX to a wide window such as +/-(LIMITS.x + 25) so the lander stays centred at any range; keep the existing ground clamp (sy via groundY) untouched.

minorInfoFindings.title: Simulation config duplicated in index.html: record period 6 and the 300 s limit are hardcoded, because sim.mjs never exports them
minorInfoFindings.detail: Spec: "physics exists in exactly one place; no duplication anywhere". run() owns `maxTime = 300` and `recordEvery = 6` as unexported parameter defaults (sim.mjs:159-164), so the browser re-implements both: `stepCount % 6 === 0` (index.html:289) and `simTime >= 300 - DT / 2` (line 291), plus the literal string "limit 300 s" in the banner (line 223) and "limit 300 s" in test.mjs's status line (test.mjs:28). If anyone changes run()'s defaults, manual-mode JSON and the on-screen limit text silently disagree. The physics constants themselves are not duplicated (verified: index.html has no 1.62/500/3000/250 literals), so this is the only drift vector.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Export `RECORD_EVERY = 6` and `MAX_SIM_TIME = 300` from sim.mjs, default run() to them, and import/use them in index.html (lines 289, 291, 223) and test.mjs (line 28).

minorInfoFindings.title: Dead export, unused imports and an unreachable crash branch
minorInfoFindings.detail: (a) `manualController` (lines 110-112) is exported but referenced nowhere in sim.mjs, index.html or test.mjs. (b) index.html imports MAX_ANGULAR_ACCEL, MAX_ANGULAR_RATE and BURN_RATE (line 130) and uses each exactly zero times outside the import statement. (c) judge()'s `OUT OF FUEL` violation (lines 146-148) can never fire: step() clamps fuel to >= 0 (lines 65-66) and the win condition is `fuel >= 0`, so `s.fuel < 0` is unsatisfiable. None of these break acceptance; they are shipped-but-unreachable surface.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Delete manualController or wire index.html's manualControl() through it; trim the three unused names from index.html's import list; keep the fuel check but comment it as a defensive assertion, or move it into the TIMEOUT/`landed` path.

minorInfoFindings.title: Constants panel text is hand-typed rather than derived from the exported constants; limits panel lacks units
minorInfoFindings.detail: PHYSICS_PANEL (lines 22-31) hardcodes display strings ('1.62 m/s^2', '500 kg', '1/60 s (fixed)') next to the real constants; all eight values currently match the spec exactly (verified against the exported bindings and against test.mjs's `physics used` line), but nothing enforces it, so the on-screen panel that exists to "confirm identical physics" can drift from the physics. Separately, the WIN LIMITS rows built from LIMITS in index.html:158-163 render `|vy| <= 3` with no unit, unlike the banner/test output which show m/s and deg.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Build PHYSICS_PANEL from the constants with template strings (e.g. `['GRAVITY', `${GRAVITY} m/s^2`]`) and `${DT === 1/60 ? '1/60 s (fixed)' : ...}`, and add units to the limits rows (m/s, m/s, deg, m).

minorInfoFindings.title: test.mjs exits 1 on a crash verdict — good practice and harmless here (exit 0 observed)
minorInfoFindings.detail: Line 39 `process.exitCode = verdict.landed ? 0 : 1;`. For acceptance item (8) the autopilot lands (LANDED at t = 12.90 s), so `node test.mjs` returns exit 0 — confirmed by four runs. A non-zero exit only happens if the autopilot is changed and stops landing, which is exactly what a CI harness should catch, so this is a net positive, not a gap.
minorInfoFindings.fix: No change needed; optionally print the exit semantics in README.md so a reviewer doesn't mistake a future exit 1 for a broken script.

minorInfoFindings.title: Agent-harness folder .qoder/ shipped inside the delivered directory
minorInfoFindings.detail: The spec lists exactly four files (sim.mjs, index.html, test.mjs, README.md). The folder also contains .qoder/settings.local.json (two allow-listed Bash permission entries) and .qoder/sessions/d2721795-.../workflows — the build agent's own state, not app code. It is not on the non-goals list (no deploy config, no backend, no auth) and does not affect the http serving path, but it is noise in a "self-contained" deliverable.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Remove .qoder/ from the shipped folder or add it to a .gitignore before publishing.

minorInfoFindings.title: Offline serving depends on the reviewer's python3 knowing the .mjs MIME type
minorInfoFindings.detail: README.md:12-16 tells reviewers to run `python3 -m http.server 8080`. python http.server derives the Content-Type from `mimetypes`; on this machine (Python 3.14.6) `guess_type('sim.mjs')` returns `text/javascript`, so the ES-module import at index.html:131 loads. On an older python3 whose mimetypes table lacks `.mjs`, the response would be `application/octet-stream` and Chrome/Firefox refuse the module with a MIME error — the page would render an empty canvas with no obvious cause. I could not start a server in this dimension, so this is a portability observation, not a confirmed failure.
minorInfoFindings.fix: Add one line to README.md: "needs Python 3.9+ (older mimetypes has no .mjs entry); any other static server works too" — or ship a 2-line note that `sim.mjs` can be renamed `sim.js` if a reviewer hits a MIME error.

logs: audit reports received: 6/6 (physics, single-source, autopilot-crosscheck, browser, ui-spec, acceptance-critic)
